name: farm monitor: chapter 3's streams on chapter 6's node mix

classes.name: greenhouse node (Wi-Fi, MQTT or SSE session kept open)
plot node (LoRaWAN, translated by the gateway into the same records)

sources.streams: bytes per record and rows per day are chapter 3's growth table (examples/ch03/streams.json, compact JSON); key_bytes is the database key each row needs (a 10-digit ts for history, dev-ts-type for events)
sources.classes: chapter 6's farm: two greenhouse nodes on Wi-Fi for every plot node on LoRaWAN; the plot node's 10-minute frame becomes one status and one history record at the gateway; one gateway per ten plot nodes is an assumption
sources.events_sizing_years: events are kept forever (chapter 3); steady state is sized here at two years so the table has a number
sources.apps: assumptions, not measurements: one phone per ten devices, watching its ten devices two hours a day, opening a 24-hour chart (144 rows) twice a day, a quarter of the phones open at the busiest moment, one settings change a day per phone
sources.self_hosted: assumptions, not benchmarks: a 10x compression ratio for time-series rows in TimescaleDB-style columnar compression (its documentation claims 90 % and more for typical telemetry; measure yours), 1.5x disk headroom, and an instance per fleet band chosen by judgement (one small ARM instance up to 100 devices, a medium one to 10 000, two large ones beyond: broker and database apart). Operations hours a month are a guess to be replaced by your own log
